notes: States derived from the screen pattern on 17 August, not individually considered. Purpose derived from the screen name and its operations on 17 August, not from a requirement.

gaps.why: **This screen declares no operation the contracts recognise.** Nothing fills it, nothing it does is committed anywhere, and its shape below is a default rather than a reading.

components.label: Language
components.notes: The languages the venue published; the choice is stored on the device and, for a signed-in guest, as the profile's language (GST-039). Arabic mirrors every layout (CF-42).

offlineBanner.message: You're offline. Connect to the internet to book, pay, order or join a queue.
offlineBanner.shows: The moment the connection drops, on every screen, above the screen's own content.
offlineBanner.clears: By itself as soon as the connection is back, with a short "Back online" confirmation.
offlineBanner.never: Covers what is already on screen, or appears for a server error — that is the screen's own error state, and a guest told they are offline when the venue is down reconnects for nothing.
offlineBanner.provenance: Decided 12 September 2026 — guest web and guest app behave identically offline and say so with the same banner.

name: Maintenance / Upgrade Page

transitions.provenance: derived — GST-001 declares entryState.params  and GST-047 holds none of them. The edge carries nothing: GST-047 is opened from GST-001, so this edge is the way back and GST-001 keeps its own state

notes: Merged with GST-060 on 18 August. The client storyboard shows this on two boards — G7 panel 7 and G8 panel 10 — which is a **board convention for a screen every journey can land on**, not two screens. Both had the same single operation and the same purpose. **Bound 28 September** to `getTenantAppStatus.minimumAppVersion` for the forced upgrade and to `availability` and `availabilityMessage` for sold out and closed (decided 28 September, audit R073 (b)(f)).
patternReason: `getTenantAppStatus` reads one record and nothing reads a population — the screen is about that one thing
purpose: Say what is wrong in a way that tells the person whether to wait or leave.

components.label: Closed for maintenance
components.notes: The main case: `isInMaintenance` with its message and the expected-back time ("Back at 14:00"), set live on CMS-001 (DI-215).

components.label: Update the app to continue
components.notes: **Forced upgrade** (decided 28 September, audit R073 (b)): when this app's version is below `minimumAppVersion` for its platform (`ios` or `android`), the screen shows the forcedUpgrade state with a button to the store and nothing else works until the guest updates. Set live from CMS-001 through `setMaintenanceMode`.

components.label: Sold out or closed today
components.notes: **From `getTenantAppStatus.availability`** (`open`, `soldOut`, `closed`) and its `availabilityMessage`, set live from CMS-001 through `setMaintenanceMode` (decided 28 September, audit R073 (f)). `soldOut` and `closed` read differently: sold out means come another day, closed means the venue is not open. Nothing shows while it is `open`.

states.error: Could not load. Names which read failed and leaves the maintenance upgrade untouched.
states.emptyFirstRun: No maintenance upgrade yet. **Offers no create action** — this screen declares no operation that makes one — and says so rather than showing an empty table.
states.offline: **The offline banner shows instead of this page.** Being offline is the guest's connection, not the venue's — an error or maintenance page shown for a dropped signal tells a guest the venue is down.
states.forcedUpgrade: **Update required.** The app's version is below `getTenantAppStatus.minimumAppVersion` for its platform; the screen offers only the store link, because an app too old to talk to the server cannot be trusted to book or pay (decided 28 September, audit R073 (b)).
states.soldOut: **Sold out today.** `getTenantAppStatus.availability` is `soldOut`: the page says so with the tenant's `availabilityMessage` and offers another day, never a generic error (decided 28 September, audit R073 (f)).
states.closed: **Closed.** `getTenantAppStatus.availability` is `closed`: the page says the venue is not open, with the tenant's `availabilityMessage` and the opening hours from `contact` (decided 28 September, audit R073 (f)).
states.emptyNoAccess: **Nothing here needs a sign-in** (decided by Chinmay, fix before Block A starts, 2 October 2026 (GFIX-2)): the screen reads only what the tenant has published, which is public, so there is no no-access case. A host that belongs to no tenant shows the platform's neutral holding page.
states.maintenance: The venue's maintenance message and when it expects to be back; one way onward (try again at that time). Set live on CMS-001, never published.

apis.purpose: Maintenance, message and expected-back time, readable without signing in
